title: The Only One of 153 to Survive: The Full Case of Bahia Bakari and Yemenia Flight 626
description:
Case 022, the full case file. At the end of June 2009 Bahia Bakari, a twelve-year-old from the Paris area and the eldest of four children, set off with her mother, Aziza, to spend the summer with family in the Comoros; her brothers and sister stayed at home with their father. They flew from Paris via Marseille to Sana'a in Yemen, where they changed planes. The last leg, Yemenia Flight 626, an Airbus A310 with 153 people on board, reached Grande Comore at about 1.50 am on 30 June, on a dark night with a strong, gusting wind, and the approach called for the crew to circle round and land from the other side. She has said she felt the plane shaking, that nobody seemed worried, then something like an electric shock, and then nothing she can remember until she found herself in the sea. She could barely swim. She heard voices calling for help in Comorian but could see no one, could not climb onto the wreckage she found, fell asleep at some point still holding on, and held on through the night and the morning; she has said that thinking of her mother kept her going. The crew of the boat Sima Com 2 threw her a life ring that she was too exhausted to grab, so a sailor jumped in and brought her to the boat. She had a broken collarbone, burns and bruises. She believed she alone had fallen out and that the others had landed safely; in hospital she learned that the plane had crashed and that she was the only survivor. 152 people died, her mother among them. On 2 July 2009 a French government jet flew her home to Le Bourget, where her father was waiting. The investigators found nothing wrong with the aircraft; their report (2013) put the accident down to the crew's actions on the approach, which led to a stall. In 2022 a Paris court tried the airline; Bahia, then 25, testified that the hardest thing had been grieving for her mother. In September 2022 the court found the airline guilty of manslaughter and imposed the maximum fine (225,000 euros), and an appeal court upheld the verdict in 2024. Rook didn't believe it either.

Chapters follow the story in order: the sea at night, the family in Paris, the journey, the approach, the water, the night, the boat, the truth, home, the investigation, the trial.

Animated reconstruction of a true story, made with respect for the 152 people who died and for their families. The crash is not shown: the film cuts to two drawn cards for the moment she cannot remember. The aircraft, the cabin, the lounge, the business jet, the boat and every other set are generic low-poly models with no livery, name, number, flag or logo, and are not models of the real ones. Bahia, her mother, her father, her brothers and sister, the passengers, the crew, the medic, the judges and the families are simple figures; nobody's likeness is attempted. The chart of the journey and the approach diagram are drawings, not maps, and are marked as such; the cards with the investigators' findings and the verdict are Rook's summaries, not copies of any document. Staging that is reconstruction, not record: the flat in Paris and the packing, the goodbye at the door, the lounge in Sana'a, the seats they sat in and what they did on board, the island shore, the shape of the piece she held, the sky, the boat and its crew, the hospital rooms, the arrival on the apron (the weather, the ambulance, the steps and the medic), the courtroom and where anyone sat, and everything Rook does. Narration is a synthetic voice (Kokoro).

source_notes: Read for this run on 17 Nov 2026 (eight pages, through a fetch tool). Every narrated fact is on at least two of the pages read. Age: 12 on five pages (AP via CBS and Fox, africanews/AFP 2022, both Wikipedia articles; Wikipedia gives her date of birth as 15 August 1996); two first-day reports (WBUR/AP, NZ Herald) said 14. 12 is used. Flight, date and place: Yemenia Flight 626, an Airbus A310, Sana'a to Moroni, came down in the sea off Grande Comore at about 1.50 am local time on 30 June 2009 (both Wikipedia articles; the Irish Times says 2 am). 153 on board (142 passengers, 11 crew) and 152 dead: Wikipedia, WBUR, africanews, AP; the NZ Herald alone says 151 others, an early count. She was travelling with her mother from Paris to visit family: WBUR, Irish Times, africanews, Wikipedia. 'She just found herself in the water': her own words as quoted by her father on WBUR and the NZ Herald, and her 2022 testimony (africanews). 'Can barely swim': WBUR, Irish Times, NZ Herald, Wikipedia. Voices in the dark that she could not see: WBUR, Irish Times, NZ Herald, africanews, Wikipedia. She held a piece of debris and could not climb onto it: africanews (her testimony) and the rescue crew's report quoted by AP ('trying to get on to a piece of wood or plastic'); what the piece was is not established (she said 'I grabbed on to something but I don't know what'), so the fuselage panel with window holes is staging. Rough seas: AP (waves up to 16 feet in the search area), Irish Times, NZ Herald, Wikipedia. Hours in the water: pages disagree, from about nine (her memoir, per Wikipedia, with a rescue at about 11 am) to more than thirteen (French officials at the time); the narration says only 'all night, then all morning', which holds in every version, and no figure is shown. The boat Sima Com 2: AP (CBS and Fox) and both Wikipedia articles. A life ring was thrown and she could not take hold of it: AP, WBUR, Irish Times, NZ Herald, Wikipedia. A sailor went into the water for her: all of those pages; his name differs (Maturaffi Selemane Libounah on AP and Wikipedia; early reports named Sgt Said Abdilai), so he is not named. Blankets and warm sugared water: WBUR, Irish Times, NZ Herald; AP has bed covers; Wikipedia has blankets and a hot drink. She believed that she alone had fallen out and that the others, her mother included, had arrived safely: her 2022 testimony (africanews: 'convinced that I was the only one who fell') and her memoir as summarised on Wikipedia. She learned in hospital that the plane had crashed and that she was the only survivor: africanews (a psychologist told her) and Wikipedia. Who told her and in which hospital are not narrated; the woman in a white coat is a generic figure. Things kept out because they rest on one page or are disputed: that she had no life jacket; that she fell asleep holding on; the taste of fuel; a ship that passed without seeing her; her injuries (pages differ beyond a broken collarbone and hypothermia); the cause of the crash and the trial; the film offer. Staging choices that are not facts: the shape and colour of the wreckage and debris; a dark, starlit sky (no page read verbatim gives the sky); the sunrise shot; the look of the boat, its crew and their clothes; where on the boat she sat; the ring's flight; the hospital room; the empty chair; the two drawn cards (they show her belief, and are headed WHAT SHE BELIEVED); her clothes and hair; everything Rook does. LONG-FORM ADDITIONS, read on 18 Nov 2026 through a fetch tool (all pages below loaded; Skybrary did not and is not used). Family and trip: eldest of four, her three siblings stayed home with their father, her mother Aziza, routed Paris-Marseille-Sana'a-Comoros to spend the summer with relatives (NBC/AP 2009, Washington Times/AP 2009, Wikipedia); born in Evry (Wikipedia only, not narrated). Change of planes at Sana'a: both Wikipedia articles and the NBC/AP route; the aircraft types are not narrated. 153 on board: as in the Short. Approach: about 1.50 am local (FlightGlobal 2009 citing Airbus, Wikipedia; ASN and BAAA give 01:54, so the label says ABOUT 1.50 AM and the narration says close to two in the morning); a night approach with strong southerly winds gusting to about 30-38 kt (FlightGlobal 2009, ASN, BAAA, AP via Himalayan Times quoting a Yemeni official at 40 mph); no moon (Wikipedia, both articles, moonset 00:23); a circle-to-land manoeuvre to land on the opposite runway (FlightGlobal 2009, ASN, Wikipedia; FlightGlobal 2013 standfirst: a circling approach at night). Her memories: the turbulence that nobody reacted to, something like an electric shock, the black hole in her memory, the taste of fuel, voices calling for help in Comorian, falling asleep holding the debris, thinking of her mother (her 2022 testimony as reported by AFP on africanews and The National; the electric feeling also in her 2009 account relayed by minister Joyandet on NBC and the Washington Times; falling asleep also from her father in 2009, NBC). 'She can't see her mother anywhere': her father in 2009 ('afraid when she couldn't see her mama', NBC and Washington Times). Too exhausted to grab the ring: Wikipedia; the Short's sources say she could not take hold of it. Injuries: broken collarbone, burns, bruises (NBC, Washington Times, Wikipedia; a broken pelvis or hip appears only on Wikipedia and Al Jazeera and is not narrated). Return: Thursday 2 July 2009 on a French government Falcon 900 with the cooperation minister, landing at Le Bourget, met by her father Kassim, who hugged her gently because of her collarbone (NBC, Washington Times; Wikipedia agrees on jet, minister, airport and father). Investigation: nothing wrong with the aircraft and inappropriate crew actions leading to a stall that could not be recovered (AFP via africanews and The National, ASN, BAAA, Wikipedia; report published in 2013: FlightGlobal 2 July 2013, BAAA June 2013, Wikipedia). Trial: opened in Paris in May 2022; she testified on 23 May 2022 at 25; the hardest thing has been grieving for her mother (AFP via africanews and The National; Al Jazeera). Verdict: September 2022, guilty of involuntary homicide (manslaughter), the maximum fine of 225,000 euros (Al Jazeera, The New Arab, Wikipedia; AFP before the verdict gives the maximum); upheld on appeal in September 2024 (The New Arab, Wikipedia). Kept out: the crew's names, the pilots' training findings and the runway-lights point (prosecution and court statements, kept out to avoid detail the film cannot show fairly); civil damages; the recorders' recovery; the memoir; the film offer; the hospital names; President Sarkozy's visit. Staging choices that are not facts: see the description.

experiments.spine: v2 kept from the Short: cold open on her at the wreckage, Rook's doubt on his panel in the scene. The long form then goes back to Paris (the Short had no room for the family, the journey or the approach) and runs forward to the trial; the jump is carried by the label PARIS, JUNE 2009.
experiments.rehook: At 50% (81.5 s of 164.5 s): 'Then, a boat... and this is where it nearly goes wrong.', then the ring she cannot grab.
experiments.learnings: plan/learnings.json asks long-forms for a stronger mid-video reversal and a shorter setup: the setup before the water is about 50 s and is told forward with a new image every 2.7 s on average; the reversal (she believes the others landed safely) lands at 62%.
experiments.rook: No jokes anywhere in this film. Detective actions: listening into the dark (22), pointing out the boat (28), reading the safety card (11), holding his hat in the wind on the island (12). He takes his hat off for her mother (43, 56) and puts it back on only for the sign-off. Mannerisms: the shed feather (4), brim low (5).
experiments.ending: 'Case closed.' (the Short loops; the long form closes the file on Rook's board).

quality_gate.method: Round 1: low-res contact sheet of all 50 3D shots plus a composite sheet of cards, captions and labels. Found and fixed: the camera inside the jet's wing on the apron (two shots) and inside the ambulance; the cabin shell open on one side; no back wall in the courtroom; the witness out of frame in the testimony and verdict shots (camera aimed too high); the window shot looking at a wall; a sheet of paper scaled into a white block in front of the judge; judges facing away from the room; Rook hidden in the lounge and seated behind a seat back in the cabin; passengers blocking her and her mother; flat and doorway too wide; the island too dark and Rook a speck; text running off the right edge on four cards; the father facing away from her in the hug. Round 2: re-rendered the 14 changed shots and checked them. Round 3: full rehearsal (384x216, 4 samples, 3D at 6 fps, composited at 12 fps with captions, labels, overlays, inserts and sound), reviewed as a 1 fps sheet of the whole video: the gate failed on five static stretches (doorway, route card, island and approach card, shock and black cards, testimony); fixed in the film (camera moves, a longer walk, card push and sway, brighter moving wind, a moving glow and more drift on the black card, a gesture in the testimony), never in the gate. Round 4: second rehearsal, one static stretch left (testimony), plus the camera starting outside the courtroom walls in two shots because of the swing, the verdict card under the caption band, two labels too long for the pop-in. Fixed. Round 5: third rehearsal, gate PASS, the changed stretches reviewed at 2 fps; thumbnail rendered twice and reframed.
quality_gate.gate_result: Local gate PASS on the last rehearsal: 60 shots, mean 2.74 s, longest 4.51 s, first shot 1.79 s with an impact at 0.03 s; Rook acting in 22 of 60 shots (37%); -14.7 LUFS, peak -1.1 dBFS, voice 20.1 dB over the bed; closest match to any earlier episode 0.83 (shot 49, the empty sea, against r019-adilang-long; limit 0.93). Duration 164.5 s (2 min 45 s), 535 words in 22 segments. The rehearsal's fingerprint file was deleted, not committed.
quality_gate.checked: Every kind in the storyboard exists in world3d.SHOTS3D or scenes.SHOTS; HOST lists only kinds where Rook is placed (bahia_look was taken out of HOST when he was framed out of it); no kind used more than twice, none twice in a row. Re-hook at 50%. Two hush shots. On-screen dates, names and figures checked against the sources: 30 JUNE 2009, OFF GRANDE COMORE, PARIS, JUNE 2009, BAHIA BAKARI, 12, ELDEST OF FOUR, AZIZA, PARIS / MARSEILLE / SANA'A / MORONI, CHANGE PLANES, SANA'A, YEMEN, 153 ON BOARD, GRANDE COMORE, ABOUT 1.50 AM, NO MOON, GUSTING WIND, SIMA COM 2, BROKEN COLLARBONE, BURNS, 152 DIED, 2 JULY 2009, LE BOURGET, PARIS, REPORT 2013, NO FAULT FOUND, A STALL, PARIS, MAY 2022, BAHIA BAKARI, 25, SEPTEMBER 2022, GUILTY OF MANSLAUGHTER, 225,000 EUROS, UPHELD ON APPEAL 2024, 152 DIED. 1 LIVED., 1 SURVIVOR. The crash is not shown; no victim is shown in the water; nothing graphic. No livery, flag, logo, lettering or likeness.
quality_gate.not_met: No playback at speed and no listening: the audio was measured, not heard. No local frame at 1280x720 except the thumbnail. The 13-category score is from stills and rehearsal sheets. The window shot (14) is mostly dark by design and reads weakly at low resolution. The HUD label pops in at 1.6x scale for 0.2 s (engine behaviour) and the longest labels touch the frame edge during that pop. The cloud render is the first full-resolution, 60 fps pass and runs the real gate.

review.weakest: The cabin shots are crowded with seat backs; the window shot is mostly dark; the courtroom is one brown tone; figures' hands cannot hold things convincingly (the cup, the paper); Rook is seen from behind in two shots. Narration and sound were measured, not heard.
